title: [YouPass Collect] - Spending on different products: 2010 vs 2014
prompt: The chart below shows the spending (in dollars) per household in the US on five different products in 2010 and 2014. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the amount of money spent per household in the United States on five types of products, namely Food, Clothes, Books, Smartphones, and Toiletries in 2010 and 2014.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, spending on most products increased over the four-year period, with the exception of Books, which saw a significant decline, and Clothes, which remained stable. Additionally, Food expenditure was consistently the highest in both years, while Books recorded the lowest figures.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding products that witnessed growth, in 2010, American households spent approximately $3,700 on Food, which was the highest figure among all categories. Meanwhile, Smartphones and Toiletries recorded lower amounts of around $2,000 and $1,900, respectively. By 2014, the spending on Food had risen significantly to roughly $4,400, representing an increase of $700 and the most substantial growth among all categories. A similar upward trend was observed in Smartphones, with its figure climbing by the same margin to approximately $2,700. Toiletries, on the other hand, experienced only a marginal growth of $100, reaching about $2,000 at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining categories, Clothes accounted for around $2,500 in 2010, making it the second-highest expenditure. Interestingly, this figure remained virtually unchanged four years later. In stark contrast, Books was the only product to experience a decline, with its spending dropping sharply from about $1,000 to just $500 over the same period, representing a fall of 50%.
